title: Sowing buckwheat shoots
subtitle: How to sow a buckwheat shoot tray — seed selection, density, and blackout weight
excerpt: Buckwheat shoots require unhulled seed: the intact triangular grain with the hull in place. Hulled buckwheat groats will not germinate. Sow densely at 100 to 150 g per 25 cm tray, press into the medium, and blackout under a 500 g to 1 kg weight to aid hull separation.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Buckwheat grain with the outer hull intact — the dark green or dark brown triangular seed used for microgreen growing. Unhulled buckwheat still contains the embryo and can germinate. It is distinct from hulled buckwheat groats, which are the pale cream inner kernels used for porridge and cooking. Groats cannot germinate.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. For buckwheat, a heavier weight than usual is used during this phase: the weight causes the seed hull to separate from the emerging cotyledon as the shoot pushes upward against resistance.

content.text: Sowing buckwheat shoots requires checking that the seed is the right type before anything else: it must be unhulled buckwheat with the outer hull intact. Hulled buckwheat groats (the pale seeds used in porridge) have had the hull and the embryo removed in processing and will not germinate.

One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray. A second tray for the blackout cover. Seed compost. Unhulled buckwheat: 100 to 150 g per tray (buckwheat is large and heavy; the seed rate is much higher than for small-seed crops). A flat piece of card for pressing. A weight of 500 g to 1 kg for the blackout phase.

is dark (green-grey or dark brown) and has a triangular faceted shape. The hull gives it a rough, slightly ridged texture. If the seed is pale cream and smooth, it is hulled groats and will not germinate. Buy from a microgreen seed supplier or a whole food retailer that stocks raw buckwheat groats labelled as unhulled or for sprouting.
Step 2: pre-dampen seed compost and fill the tray to within 1 cm of the rim. Level the surface.

Step 3: scatter buckwheat at 100 to 150 g per tray. Spread the seed in a dense single layer; the triangular seeds should be touching but not stacked. Use your hands to distribute evenly across the surface. Do not cover the seed with compost.
Step 4: press firmly with the flat base of the second tray across the whole surface.

: stack the second tray on top and add 500 g to 1 kg of weight. The weight is heavier than for other microgreen crops. As buckwheat shoots push upward during germination, the resistance from the weight causes the seed hull to peel away from the emerging cotyledon. Less weight means more hulls cling to the seedlings after the blackout phase ends. Leave for three to four days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with buckwheat shoots.

items.cause: Hulled groats used instead of unhulled seed.
items.fix: Check the seed colour and texture: unhulled buckwheat is dark with a textured hull; groats are pale and smooth. Replace the seed with correctly-specified unhulled buckwheat.

items.symptom: All hulls still attached after blackout phase
items.fix: Increase the blackout weight to 1 to 1.5 kg on the next attempt. The hull-separation mechanism depends on the shoot pushing against resistance.

items.symptom: Medium dries out quickly despite pre-dampening
items.cause: The dense sowing of large seed absorbs a lot of the medium moisture rapidly.
items.fix: Pre-dampen the compost more thoroughly before filling. If the medium feels dry at day 2, bottom-water once by setting the tray in 2 cm of water for 10 minutes.
